73225.e: Apprentices must do everything they can to reach the training goal, follow instructions and work carefully (Art. 345 Code of Obligations).
73225.m: Apprentices follow instructions and work carefully.

73226.q: Apprentices lead a youth camp during the holidays. How much extra time off can they take for this each year?
73226.e: Anyone up to the age of 30 who helps with youth work unpaid, for example as a camp leader, can take up to one week of youth leave per year.
73226.m: For youth work you get up to one week of youth leave per year.

73227.q: Is apprentices' pay set by law in Switzerland?
a: No, there are only recommendations from the industries
Yes, it is the same as for adults
73227.e: There is no legal minimum wage for apprentices. Many professional associations give pay recommendations.
73227.m: Apprentice pay is based on industry recommendations.

73228.q: What must apprentices keep regularly at the company to record their learning?
73228.e: In the learning log, apprentices record what they have learned. The trainer checks it.

73229.q: What is the document called in which the training company regularly records the apprentice's progress?
73229.e: In the training report, the company regularly records, usually each semester, how the apprentice is developing.
73229.m: The training report is used to discuss progress regularly.

73230.q: Is night work generally allowed for apprentices under 18?
73230.e: Night work is generally forbidden for young people under 18. There are exceptions only for certain jobs where it is needed for the training, for example in a bakery.
73230.m: Young people are generally not allowed to work at night.

73921.q: You knocked over the vase by accident. What is the honest thing to do?
73921.e: Being honest means telling the truth, even when you have made a mistake. Accidents can happen to anyone.
73921.m: Owning up to a mistake is honest.

73922.q: What is it called when someone says something untrue on purpose?
73922.e: A lie is something you say that you know is not true. You want to trick others with it.
73922.m: A lie is untrue on purpose.

73923.q: You find someone else's purse in the playground. What do you do?
73923.e: Things you find belong to someone else. If you hand them in, you help the owner get them back.

73924.q: Why is honesty important for friends?
73924.e: When friends are honest, they know they can believe each other. That is how trust grows.

73925.q: Your friend cheated in a game and you saw it. What is fair and honest?
73925.e: If you calmly mention the cheating, you stay honest and fair. Laughing or cheating yourself makes it worse.
73925.m: Calmly speak up about things that are unfair.

73926.q: What often happens when you tell one lie?
73926.e: One lie often leads to more lies so that it isn't found out. That quickly becomes tiring.
73926.m: One lie often leads to more lies.

73927.q: Which sentence is honest if you forgot your homework?
73927.e: Only the first sentence says what really happened. The other sentences are not true.
73927.m: Honest means saying what really happened.

a: A reason that isn't quite true
73928.e: With an excuse, you try to talk your way out of something. The reason you give is often not true.
73928.m: An excuse distracts from the truth.

73929.q: What makes someone a good friend?
73929.e: Good friends support each other, even when things are difficult. They are there for each other.

73930.q: Your friend is sad. What can you do?
73930.e: Asking shows that the other person matters to you. Often just listening helps.

73931.q: A new child is in the class and doesn't know anyone. What is kind?
a: Copy them to make fun of them
73931.e: New children often feel unsure. An invitation to play helps them fit in.
73931.m: New children are happy to be invited.

73932.q: Can you be friends with more than one child?
a: No, only with children from your own class
No, only with your own brothers and sisters
73932.e: You can have lots of friends. Every friendship is something special.
73932.m: You can have lots of friends.

73933.q: Your friend tells you a secret that doesn't harm anyone. What do you do?
a: Write it down and hand it out
73933.e: Keeping a secret shows that you can be trusted. Then your friend can tell you things later on too.

73934.q: Which kind of secret should you tell an adult you trust?
73934.e: Secrets where someone is afraid or being hurt can and should be told to someone you trust. That is not betrayal.

73935.q: How do you show a friend that you like them?
73935.e: Spending time together shows that someone matters to you. Playing, talking and laughing make a friendship stronger.

73936.q: Your friend made a mistake while drawing and is sad. What do you say?
73936.e: Encouraging words comfort your friend and show that you are on her side. Everyone makes mistakes.
73936.m: Good friends cheer each other up.

73937.e: A compliment is a friendly remark, for example “You've drawn that really well”. It makes others happy.

73938.q: You have three apples and your friend has none. What is kind?
73938.e: When you share, you think of others too. Then you both have something.

73939.q: You share 8 jelly sweets fairly with a friend. How many does each of you get?
73939.e: 8 divided by 2 is 4. That way you each have the same number.
73939.m: When you share fairly, everyone gets the same amount.

73940.q: Two children want the same swing. What is a good solution?
73940.e: Taking turns is a way of sharing. Everyone gets a go.

73941.q: Apart from things, what else can you share?
73941.e: You can also share time, ideas and joy with others. That costs nothing.
73941.m: You can share time and joy too.

73942.q: Can you just take something that belongs to someone else to share it?
a: Yes, if the owner is away
73942.e: Sharing something that isn't yours is only OK with permission. Otherwise you are taking something away from someone.
73942.m: Only share other people's things with permission.

73943.q: You cut a pizza into 4 equal pieces for 4 children. How many pieces does each child get?
73943.e: 4 pieces for 4 children is 1 piece per child. That is fair.
73943.m: The same number of pieces is fair.

73944.q: How do you politely ask if you can borrow something?
73944.e: Saying “please” is asking politely. Then the other person can decide for themselves.

73945.q: What do you do with a borrowed book?
73945.e: Borrowed things belong to someone else. You look after them well and give them back.

73946.q: In a race, one child starts too early. Is that fair?
a: No, everyone should start at the same time
Yes, fast people can start earlier
Yes, if they really want to win
73946.e: Starting too early gives you an unfair advantage. Everyone should start running at the same time.
73946.m: In a fair race, everyone starts at the same time.

73947.q: How does a fair winner behave?
73947.e: If you win and stay friendly, you don't hurt anyone. Laughing at others spoils the fun for everyone.

73948.q: What is fair behaviour in sport called?
73948.e: Fair play means keeping to the rules and respecting your opponent.

73949.q: How can you fairly decide who starts in a game?
73949.e: When you roll a dice, every child has the same chance. That is fair.
73949.m: Rolling a dice gives everyone the same chance.

73950.q: A child can't run because of a plaster cast. What is fair in the game?
73950.e: Being fair sometimes means being considerate. With a suitable job, the child can still join in.
73950.m: Fair is when everyone can join in.

73951.q: What is a foul in football?
73951.e: A foul is breaking the rules of the game, for example tripping someone up. There is a penalty for it.
73951.m: A foul is against the rules.

73952.q: A child has fallen over and is crying. What do you do?
73952.e: Helpful people look after others when they need help. If someone is hurt, you fetch an adult.
73952.m: Someone who falls over needs help.

73953.q: Who do you call on 144 in Switzerland after a bad accident?
73953.e: In Switzerland, 144 is the emergency number for the ambulance service, the rescue service with the ambulance.
73953.m: You reach the ambulance service on 144.

73954.q: What is the emergency number for the fire brigade in Switzerland?
73954.e: In Switzerland you reach the fire brigade on 118. You call them, for example, if there is a fire.

73955.q: Which number can children in Switzerland call when they are worried?
73955.e: The number 147 from Pro Juventute is there for children and young people. Someone listens and helps there, day and night and free of charge.
73955.m: When you're worried, the number 147 helps.

73956.q: An older man is carrying heavy bags up the stairs. What is helpful?
73956.e: If you first ask whether help is wanted, you are helpful and polite. The other person can then say yes or no.
73956.m: Offer help in a friendly way.

73957.q: How can you help at home?
73957.e: Small jobs like laying the table help the whole family. Then one person doesn't have to do everything alone.

73958.q: What do you say when someone has helped you?
73958.e: Saying “thank you” shows that you value the help. That makes the helper happy.

73959.q: How does a child who is laughing and jumping feel?
73959.e: Laughing and jumping are typical signs of joy.
73959.m: Someone who laughs is often happy.

73960.q: A child has tears in their eyes and their head is hanging down. How do they probably feel?
73960.e: Tears and a hanging head often show sadness. You can ask what is wrong.

73961.q: A child is clenching their fists and has a red face. What feeling do they probably have?
73961.e: Clenched fists and a red face are often signs of anger. You can ask the child what is wrong.

73962.q: What can help when you are very angry?
73962.e: Breathing deeply calms the body. Afterwards you can say better what is bothering you.
73962.m: Deep breaths calm you down when you're angry.

73963.q: What is the feeling called when you are frightened of something?
73963.e: Fear warns us about dangers. It is good to talk to someone about it.

73964.q: You have finished painting a difficult picture. Which feeling fits?
73964.e: When you have managed something difficult, you are proud of it.
73964.m: When you've managed something, you're proud.

73965.q: What is it called when you can feel what others are feeling?
73965.e: Empathy means you sense how someone else is feeling. Then you can help better.

73966.q: What is the feeling called when you want something that someone else has?
73966.e: You feel envy when you begrudge someone something or want it yourself. Everyone has this feeling sometimes.

73967.e: All feelings are allowed, including anger and sadness. What matters is how you deal with them.

73968.q: What helps most when two children are arguing?
73968.e: When you talk to each other, you understand what is bothering the other person. That way you find a solution.

73969.q: How do you start a sentence to say what bothers you without blaming someone?
73969.e: An “I” sentence says how you feel without attacking the other person. That way the other person listens better.

73970.q: What should you do while the other person explains in an argument?
73970.e: If you listen, you find out why the other person is upset. Then it's your turn.

73971.q: What is a solution called where both sides give in a little?
73971.e: In a compromise, everyone gets some of what they want. So in the end both are fairly happy.
73971.m: In a compromise, both give in.

73972.q: Who can help if children can't sort out their argument on their own?
73972.e: Teachers or parents can help find a solution. In some schools, trained children also help as “peacemakers”.
73972.m: In a difficult argument, get help.

73973.q: What is not a good idea in an argument?
73973.e: Violence hurts and makes the argument worse. Talking, listening or taking a break help.

73974.q: Why can a short break help in an argument?
73974.e: With a bit of distance, you get calmer. Afterwards you usually talk to each other in a friendlier way.
73974.m: A break helps everyone calm down.

73975.q: What is a person called who helps two people who are arguing to sort things out?
73975.e: A mediator helps both sides listen to each other and find a solution. They don't take sides.

73976.q: Two children want to read the same book. Which solution is peaceful?
73976.e: If both read together, both get something out of it. That way there is no argument.

73977.q: You bumped into someone by accident. What do you say?
73977.e: You say sorry even if it was an accident. That way the other person knows it wasn't on purpose.

73978.q: What is part of a good apology?
73978.e: If you apologise properly, you say what you did wrong. That shows you are sorry.

73979.q: Apart from words, how can you show you are sorry?
73979.e: If, for example, you build a tower back up after knocking it over, you put the damage right. That shows you mean it.
73979.m: Putting things right shows you are sorry.

73980.q: Someone apologises to you. What can you answer?
73980.e: Accepting an apology ends the argument. Afterwards you can play together again.

73981.q: What is it called when you no longer hold a mistake against someone?
73981.e: Forgiving means letting go of being angry. That does both people good.
73981.m: Forgiving means letting go of anger.

73982.q: What would be a bad apology?
73982.e: If you blame the other person in the same sentence, you aren't really apologising. A real apology has no “but”.

73983.q: What is it called when two people become friends again after an argument?
73983.e: When two people make up, they put their argument behind them. It often starts with an apology.
73983.m: After the argument comes making up.

73984.q: When is the best time to apologise?
a: Only when the other person asks for it
73984.e: The sooner you apologise, the sooner the anger is over.

73985.e: If you let others finish speaking, you show that their opinion matters. That is respectful.
73985.m: Letting people finish speaking is respectful.

73986.q: What do people in German-speaking Switzerland often say as a greeting?
73986.e: “Grüezi” is a common, polite greeting in German-speaking Switzerland. Greeting people shows respect.

73987.q: How do you treat other people's things respectfully?
73987.e: Other people's things belong to someone else. You handle them carefully.

73988.q: How do you show respect for nature?
73988.e: If you take your rubbish with you, you protect animals and plants. That way nature stays beautiful.
73988.m: Take your rubbish home from nature.

73989.q: A child doesn't want to be hugged. What is respectful?
73989.e: Everyone can decide for themselves who may touch them. A no must be respected.

73990.q: How do you show respect for animals?
73990.e: Animals have feelings too and can feel pain. You treat them kindly and carefully.

73991.q: What is respectful on the bus?
a: Putting your feet on the seat
73991.e: Older or injured people often find it hard to stand. Offering them your seat shows respect.

73992.e: Swear words hurt others. Respectful people don't use them.

73993.q: Why are there rules at school?
a: So that everyone gets on well together
73993.e: Rules help everyone treat each other safely and fairly. Without rules there would be more arguments.

73994.q: At which colour of traffic light can you cross the road as a pedestrian?
73994.e: At green, pedestrians may cross. At red, you have to wait.

73995.q: What do you do in Switzerland before crossing a zebra crossing?
73995.e: “Wait, look, listen, walk” (in Swiss German “Warte, luege, lose, laufe”) is the Swiss road safety rule for children. You wait, look, listen and only then cross.
73995.m: Before crossing, wait, look and listen.

73996.q: How do you show in class that you want to say something?
73996.e: If you put your hand up, you wait until it's your turn. That way everyone can talk in peace.
73996.m: If you want to say something, put your hand up.

73997.q: Who can make rules together in a class?
73997.e: Many classes have a class council. There, children and the teacher discuss rules together.
73997.m: In the class council, you make rules together.

73998.q: What often happens when nobody keeps to the rules of a game?
73998.e: Rules make sure everyone knows what applies. Without them, people argue.

73999.q: What is best to wear for your safety when cycling?
73999.e: A bike helmet protects your head if you fall. That is why it is very important.
73999.m: A bike helmet protects your head.

74000.q: What are rules called that apply to everyone in a country?
74000.e: Laws are the rules of a country. In Switzerland, parliaments pass laws, and sometimes the people vote on them too.
74000.m: Laws apply to everyone in the country.

74001.q: Which rule usually applies when playing ball in the playground?
74001.e: If nobody hits anyone on purpose, nobody gets hurt. Everyone should have fun.
74001.m: When playing, never hurt anyone on purpose.

74002.q: A child speaks a different language at home. What is right?
74002.e: In Switzerland, many families speak a different language at home. Knowing several languages is a treasure.
74002.m: Knowing several languages is a treasure.

74003.q: A child uses a wheelchair. What is kind when playing?
a: Find a game they can join in
74003.e: With a bit of imagination, you can find games that everyone can join in. Nobody should be left out.

74004.q: Why is it good that people are different?
a: We can learn from each other
74004.e: Different people have different ideas and skills. So we can learn a lot from each other.

74005.q: What is it called when someone isn't allowed to join in just because they are different?
74005.e: Excluding someone hurts and is unfair. Every child wants to belong.

74006.q: A child has a different skin colour from you. What does that mean?
74006.e: Skin colour says nothing about what a person is like. All people are worth the same.
74006.m: All people are worth the same.

74007.q: What is it called when someone is picked on on purpose again and again?
74007.e: In bullying, someone is picked on or left out on purpose over a long time. Then you must tell adults.

74008.q: What is a fixed opinion about a group called, held without knowing the people?
74008.e: A prejudice is a judgement made before you know someone. It is often wrong.
74008.m: A prejudice judges before you know someone.

a: Helping a child who is being picked on
74009.e: Being brave means doing the right thing, even when it is difficult. If you help a child who is being picked on, you stand up for others.
74009.m: Brave people do the right thing.

74010.q: Is it brave to run across the road when the light is red?
a: Yes, if your friends are watching
74010.e: Putting yourself in danger for no reason is reckless, not brave. Courage needs good sense too.
74010.m: Being reckless is not being brave.

74011.q: A child is being picked on and you don't dare step in on your own. What is brave?
74011.e: Just watching doesn't help the child who is being picked on. It is brave to get help from an adult.

74012.q: You are scared of a task but you try it anyway. What are you showing?
74012.e: Courage doesn't mean not being scared. Brave people try even though they are scared.
74012.m: Courage means trying even when you are scared.

74013.q: Is it brave to say “No” when others want to do something wrong?
a: No, you should always join in
Only if you are the biggest
74013.e: It takes courage not to join in when everyone else is doing something wrong. A clear no protects you and others.
74013.m: Saying no to something wrong takes courage.

74014.q: Which sentence is brave when a child is being laughed at?
74014.e: Standing up for a child who is being laughed at shows courage. It helps the child a lot.
74014.m: Standing up for others is brave.

74015.q: Is it brave to admit a mistake?
74015.e: Admitting mistakes takes courage, because you might get into trouble. But others trust you more for it.

74016.q: What is the opposite of brave?
74016.e: A coward is someone who is too scared to do the right thing. Brave is the opposite.
74016.m: The opposite of brave is cowardly.

a: A rule for behaviour in a group
A feeling like joy or anger
74017.e: Norms are rules of behaviour that say what is expected in a community. They often come from values.
74017.m: Norms are rules that guide our behaviour in the community.

74018.q: Which example is a value and not a norm?
a: Not smacking your lips at the table
Switching off your mobile in the cinema
74018.e: A value is something that people think is important and worth striving for, such as honesty. The other examples are concrete rules of behaviour, so they are norms.
74018.m: Values say what is important, and norms say how you should behave.

74019.q: What is a norm called that is laid down by the state as a law?
74019.e: Legal norms are made by state bodies and can be enforced with penalties. Customs and traditions, on the other hand, are based on habit.
74019.m: Legal norms are laws that the state can enforce.

74020.q: What is a group's reaction called when someone keeps to or breaks a norm?
74020.e: Sanctions can be positive, such as praise, or negative, such as a telling-off or a fine. They make sure that norms are kept.
74020.m: With sanctions, a group rewards or punishes the behaviour of its members.

74021.q: Which language does the word “ethics” come from?
74021.e: “Ethics” comes from the Greek word “ethos”, which means habit, custom or character. The philosopher Aristotle established ethics as a subject of its own.
74021.m: The word ethics goes back to the Greek word ethos.

74022.q: What is the difference between morality and ethics?
74022.e: Morality means the values and rules that people actually live by. Ethics is the study that examines morality and gives reasons for it.
74022.m: Ethics is thinking about what is morally right.

74023.q: What is a situation called in which two important values are in conflict?
74023.e: In a conflict of values, you have to weigh things up, for example between honesty and sparing a friend's feelings. Both values are important, but you can't do full justice to both.
74023.m: In a conflict of values, you have to weigh up two important values.

74024.q: Which statement about norms is true?
a: They are the same everywhere in the world
They were all taken over from animals
They only apply to a single person
74024.e: Norms depend on culture and time. What used to be seen as rude can be normal today, and in other countries some rules are different.
74024.m: Norms are not fixed for ever but change with society.

74025.q: Which value is most important when you keep a promise?
74025.e: Others can rely on people who keep their promises. Reliability creates trust in friendships and in the community.
74025.m: Keeping promises shows reliability and creates trust.

a: The inner voice that judges good and bad
The ability to calculate very fast
74026.e: Conscience is the inner awareness of whether your own actions are right or wrong. It often makes itself felt as a good or bad feeling.
74026.m: Conscience is our inner voice for right and wrong.

74027.q: What is the unpleasant feeling called after you have done something wrong?
74027.e: Pangs of conscience come when you realise that you have acted against your own values. They can lead you to apologise or put something right.
74027.m: Pangs of conscience show us that we have acted against our own values.

74028.q: Which fundamental right in the Swiss Federal Constitution protects conscience?
74028.e: Article 15 of the Federal Constitution guarantees freedom of religion and conscience. Every person may freely choose and profess their religion and their beliefs.
74028.m: Article 15 of the Federal Constitution protects freedom of religion and conscience.

74029.q: Which service can Swiss people do if they cannot do military service for reasons of conscience?
74029.e: Since 1996, anyone in Switzerland who cannot reconcile military service with their conscience can do a longer civilian service instead. It is done, for example, in hospitals, care homes or nature conservation.
74029.m: Civilian service is the alternative for those liable for military service who have a conflict of conscience.

74030.q: When does someone have a conflict of conscience?
a: When an order goes against their own conscience
When they have forgotten two pieces of homework
When they can't choose a pudding
When two friends have their birthday on the same day
74030.e: A conflict of conscience happens when you are supposed to do something that you yourself think is wrong. A famous example is Antigone from a Greek tragedy.
74030.m: A conflict of conscience happens when duty and conscience don't fit together.

74031.q: According to modern psychology, how does a person's conscience develop?
a: It is shaped by upbringing and experience
It is already complete at birth
It only appears at the age of 60
It is decided by the weather alone
74031.e: Children learn from parents, teachers and other people what is right and wrong. This forms their conscience over many years.
74031.m: Conscience grows through upbringing, role models and your own experiences.

74032.q: What does the expression “to have a clear conscience” mean?
a: You know you have done nothing wrong
You have had a thorough wash
You have saved a lot of money
74032.e: Someone with a clear or good conscience believes they have acted rightly. The opposite is a guilty conscience.
74032.m: You have a clear conscience if you are sure you have done nothing wrong.

74033.q: Which reformer is said to have declared in Worms in 1521 that his conscience was captive to the Word of God?
74033.e: At the Diet of Worms in 1521, Martin Luther refused to take back his writings. In doing so, he appealed to his conscience.
74033.m: In Worms in 1521, Martin Luther appealed to his conscience.

74034.q: What does it mean to take responsibility for an action?
74034.e: Taking responsibility means standing by what you have done and dealing with the consequences. That includes admitting mistakes.
74034.m: Responsibility means answering for the consequences of your own actions.

74035.q: From what age can a child in Switzerland be punished under juvenile criminal law?
74035.e: The Swiss Juvenile Criminal Law applies to young people from their 10th birthday. For young people, protection and education come first.
74035.m: In Switzerland, criminal responsibility begins at 10.

74036.q: At what age are you an adult in the eyes of the law in Switzerland?
74036.e: In Switzerland you are an adult at 18. This is called coming of age. Then you can, for example, vote in ballots and elections.
74036.m: In Switzerland, you come of age at 18.

74037.q: According to environmental ethics, who else are people responsible for?
74037.e: What we do today affects the lives of the people of tomorrow. That is why the philosopher Hans Jonas called for responsibility for the future of the Earth.
74037.m: We are responsible for the future of the Earth.

74038.q: What is the offence called when you don't help a person in mortal danger, even though you reasonably could?
74038.e: Article 128 of the Swiss Criminal Code punishes anyone who does not help a person in immediate mortal danger, even though they could reasonably be expected to. Often it is enough to call for help.
74038.m: Anyone who doesn't help a person in mortal danger, though they could, is committing an offence.

74039.q: What is part of our responsibility towards future generations?
a: Producing as much rubbish as possible
Cutting down all the forests quickly
74039.e: If you act sustainably, you only use as much as allows later generations to live well too. This includes, for example, saving energy and avoiding waste.
74039.m: Sustainability means thinking about the people of tomorrow too.

74040.q: Who is responsible in a class for a device that has been borrowed together?
74040.e: Anyone who uses or borrows something must handle it carefully and report damage. Shared responsibility doesn't mean that nobody has to care.
74040.m: If you use something together, you are responsible for it together.

74041.q: What is the effect called where, in a large group, often nobody feels responsible?
74041.e: With diffusion of responsibility, everyone thinks someone else will act. That is why in groups sometimes nobody helps, even though many people are watching.
74041.m: When many people are watching, responsibility is often spread so thinly that nobody acts.

74042.q: Which objects does Lady Justice, the figure of justice, usually hold in her hands?
74042.e: The scales stand for careful weighing up, the sword for enforcing the law. Lady Justice can often be seen on fountains, for example on the Justice Fountain in Bern.
74042.m: Lady Justice carries scales for weighing up and a sword for enforcing the law.

74043.q: Why does Lady Justice often wear a blindfold?
a: She judges without regard to who someone is
She is dazzled by the light
She is playing blind man's buff
74043.e: The blindfold shows that the law applies equally to everyone. Wealth, background or appearance should not influence the judgement.
74043.m: Lady Justice's blindfold stands for judging without regard to who someone is.

74044.q: What is justice called where everyone gets what they need?
74044.e: With justice according to need, whoever needs more gets more, for example a sick child gets more help. With justice according to merit, on the other hand, you get what you have earned.
74044.m: Justice according to need depends on what someone really needs.

74045.q: What is justice called where everyone should have the same starting conditions?
74045.e: Equal opportunities means that everyone should get the same chances, for example in access to education. What you make of them then depends on you.
74045.m: Equal opportunities means the same chances for everyone.

74046.q: What do you do in the thought experiment called the “veil of ignorance”?
a: Choose rules without knowing what place you will get yourself
Hide your own opinion from others
Decide all rules by rolling a dice
74046.e: If you don't know whether you will later be rich or poor, healthy or ill, you are more likely to choose rules that are fair for everyone. The idea comes from the philosopher John Rawls.
74046.m: The veil of ignorance helps to find rules that are fair for everyone.

74047.q: Three children share 12 biscuits equally. How many biscuits does each child get?
74047.e: 12 divided by 3 is 4. When things are shared equally, each child gets the same amount.
74047.m: When things are shared equally, each person gets the same share.

74048.q: What does justice according to merit mean?
a: Those who achieve more get more
Those who need more get more
Those who are older get more
74048.e: With justice according to merit, the reward depends on what someone has achieved. With justice according to need, what counts is what someone needs.
74048.m: Justice according to merit rewards what you have achieved.

74049.q: Which Swiss court is the highest court in the country?
74049.e: The Federal Supreme Court has its main seat in Lausanne. As the court of last instance, it reviews judgements of the cantonal courts.
74049.m: The Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne is the highest court in Switzerland.

74050.q: How does the Golden Rule go in its well-known short form?
a: Treat others as you want to be treated
The early bird catches the worm
74050.e: The Golden Rule asks us to treat others the way we would like to be treated ourselves. It is seen as one of the oldest principles of morality.
74050.m: Treat others the way you would like to be treated.

74051.q: Why is the Golden Rule called a rule of reciprocity?
a: You put yourself in the other person's position
You take turns playing a game
74051.e: The Golden Rule asks you to check your own actions from the point of view of the person affected. This change of perspective is at its heart.
74051.m: The Golden Rule asks you to put yourself in the other person's position.

74052.q: Which Chinese thinker already knew a form of the Golden Rule around 500 BC?
74052.e: Confucius said, in essence: what you do not wish for yourself, do not do to others. The rule appears in many cultures and religions.
74052.m: Even Confucius taught a form of the Golden Rule.

74053.q: In which part of the Bible is the Golden Rule found as part of the Sermon on the Mount?
74053.e: In Matthew 7:12, Jesus says that you should do to others as you would like to be treated yourself. This passage is part of the Sermon on the Mount.
74053.m: The Golden Rule is found in the Sermon on the Mount in the Gospel of Matthew.

74054.q: Which action follows the Golden Rule?
a: Showing a new child around the school
Leaving someone out of a game
74054.e: Someone who is new is happy to get help and make friends. You would want that kind of help yourself in that situation.
74054.m: Following the Golden Rule, you help others the way you would like to be helped.

74055.q: In how many world religions can you find a form of the Golden Rule?
a: In all the major world religions
74055.e: The Golden Rule is found in Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism and Buddhism. That is why it is seen as a shared principle of many cultures.
74055.m: The Golden Rule links many religions and cultures of the world.

74056.q: Which behaviour breaks the Golden Rule?
a: Giving away a secret you wouldn't want given away yourself
74056.e: Nobody wants their own secrets to be passed on. That is why you shouldn't do it to others either.
74056.m: What you wouldn't want to happen to you, don't do to others.

74057.q: What is the counterpart to the Golden Rule called, which says “tit for tat”?
74057.e: With the principle of retaliation, like is answered with like, including bad with bad. The Golden Rule, on the other hand, asks you to take the first good step yourself.
74057.m: The Golden Rule goes beyond simple “tit for tat”.

a: Respecting other religions, even if you believe differently
Everyone must belong to the same religion
Religions may only be practised in secret
You may not talk about any religion
74058.e: Religious tolerance means that every person may live their faith freely. The philosopher John Locke already demanded that the state should force no one into a faith.
74058.m: Religious tolerance means respecting other faiths.

74059.q: Which Latin word does “tolerance” come from?
74059.e: The Latin verb “tolerare” means to bear or to endure. The word tolerance comes from it.
74059.m: Tolerance comes from the Latin word tolerare, to bear.

74061.q: Which behaviour shows tolerance towards another religion?
a: Respecting that a classmate celebrates different festivals
Wanting to ban other people's festivals
74061.e: Tolerant people let others keep their customs and festivals. You can even ask curious questions and learn a lot.
74061.m: Tolerance means respecting other people's customs.

74062.q: According to a widely held view, where does tolerance end?
a: Where the rights of others are violated
Where someone speaks a different language
Where someone listens to different music
74062.e: Tolerance doesn't mean accepting everything. Violence, stirring up hatred or attacks on human dignity do not have to be tolerated.
74062.m: Tolerance ends where others are hurt or threatened.

74063.q: Why were there many wars of religion in Europe after the Reformation?
a: Because Catholics and Protestants did not tolerate each other
Because there were too few churches
Because everyone had the same religion
74063.e: After the Reformation, Catholics and Protestants often fought against each other. Only laws of toleration, such as the Edict of Nantes in France, brought more peace.
74063.m: A lack of tolerance once led to wars of religion.

74064.q: Which attitude is the opposite of tolerance?
74064.e: Intolerant people reject other opinions, religions or ways of life and often don't want to accept them. This can lead to people being excluded.
74064.m: Intolerance is rejecting everything that is different.

74065.q: How do you show tolerance in a class discussion?
a: You listen and let others finish speaking
74065.e: If you listen and let others finish speaking, you show respect for their opinion. Afterwards you can calmly give your own opinion.
74065.m: Listening and letting others finish speaking shows tolerance.

a: The courage to stand up for others and for values in everyday life
The courage of soldiers in war
74066.e: People show civil courage when they don't look away from injustice but act, even when it is unpleasant. The term combines “civil”, meaning to do with citizens, and “courage”.
74066.m: Civil courage means bravely standing up for others and for justice in everyday life.

74067.q: What is most important for civil courage in a dangerous situation?
a: Getting help without putting yourself in danger
Throwing yourself into a fight alone
74067.e: You should help, but not put yourself in danger. Often the most effective thing is to speak to other people and call the police.
74067.m: In danger, the best way to help is to get help and protect yourself.

74068.q: As a witness to an attack, how can you best help the police later?
a: Tidy up the scene straight away
Never say anything about it again
74068.e: Exact observations such as clothing, height or the direction they ran off in help the police to solve the case. Giving evidence as a witness is also a form of civil courage.
74068.m: Watching carefully and giving evidence as a witness shows civil courage.

74069.q: In 1938, the St Gallen police officer Paul Grüninger let Jewish refugees into Switzerland despite a ban. What did he show by doing this?
74069.e: Grüninger got round the rules to save persecuted people. He was dismissed for it and was only fully rehabilitated in 1995.
74069.m: Paul Grüninger showed civil courage when he saved persecuted people.

74070.q: During the Second World War, the Swiss diplomat Carl Lutz issued letters of protection in Budapest. Who did he save with them?
a: Tens of thousands of persecuted Jews
74070.e: Carl Lutz was vice-consul in Budapest in 1944. With his letters of protection, he saved tens of thousands of Jewish people from deportation.
74070.m: With courage and letters of protection, Carl Lutz saved many lives.

74071.q: Which African American woman refused to give up her seat on a bus in Montgomery in 1955?
74071.e: Rosa Parks was arrested because she would not give up her seat to a white passenger. Her courage sparked a big bus boycott.
74071.m: With her courage, Rosa Parks became a symbol of the civil rights movement.

74072.q: What was the name of Sophie and Hans Scholl's resistance group against National Socialism?
74072.e: The White Rose handed out leaflets against the Nazi regime in 1942 and 1943. Sophie and Hans Scholl were executed in 1943.
74072.m: The White Rose stands for the brave resistance of young people.

74073.q: What can you do first about bullying in your class?
74073.e: Teachers or other adults can step in and help. Getting help is not telling tales, it is civil courage.
74073.m: Reporting bullying shows civil courage and helps the victim.

74074.q: Which young Pakistani woman campaigned for girls' education despite death threats and received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014?
74074.e: Malala Yousafzai was badly injured in an attack in 2012 but carried on with her campaign. At 17 she became the youngest winner of the Nobel Peace Prize.
74074.m: Malala Yousafzai showed great courage in fighting for the right to education.

74075.q: What is a simplified, fixed picture of a whole group called?
74075.e: A stereotype is a generalising idea, for example “Everyone from country X is lazy”. Such pictures don't do justice to individual people.
74075.m: Stereotypes are boxes into which whole groups are put.

74076.q: What is a person or group called who is unfairly blamed for problems?
74076.e: The term comes from an old ritual in which a goat symbolically carried the people's guilt into the desert. Today it means people who are wrongly blamed for problems.
74076.m: Someone who is made a scapegoat is unfairly blamed for others.

74077.q: What is a hostile attitude towards people from other countries or cultures called?
74077.e: Xenophobia, also called hostility towards foreigners, is often based on prejudice against strangers. It can lead to exclusion and disadvantage.
74077.m: Xenophobia often grows from prejudice against strangers.

74078.q: What helps most to break down prejudices?
a: Always staying in your own group
74078.e: When you get to know others personally, you notice that they are different and don't match the prejudice. Meeting and talking in this way breaks down mistrust.
74078.m: Meeting people is the best remedy for prejudice.

74079.q: Why are prejudices often hard to change?
a: People mainly notice examples that confirm them
They are in every law book
74079.e: People tend to notice what confirms their opinion and overlook examples against it. This confirmation bias keeps prejudices alive.
74079.m: Prejudices last because we like to notice only confirming examples.

74080.q: Which statement is a generalisation and therefore a possible prejudice?
a: “Everyone who wears glasses is a swot.”
74080.e: The word “everyone” treats a whole group as the same without knowing the individuals. The other sentences describe facts that can be checked.
74080.m: Statements about a group with “everyone” are often prejudices.

74081.q: Where do children often pick up their first prejudices?
a: From the people around them, such as family and the media
From the blueprint of their genes
74081.e: Prejudices are not something you are born with; they are learned. Children often pick them up without realising from people around them or from the media.
74081.m: Prejudices are not inborn but learned.

a: Treating people worse because of a characteristic
74082.e: With discrimination, people are treated worse because of, for example, their origin, religion, skin colour or disability. That is unfair and often forbidden.
74082.m: Discrimination means unfairly treating people worse because of a characteristic.

74083.q: What does the Swiss Federal Constitution say about discrimination?
a: It is only allowed for companies
74083.e: The Federal Constitution states that all people are equal before the law. Nobody may be discriminated against, for example because of their origin, language or disability.

74084.q: Which Swiss law is meant to prevent people with disabilities from being disadvantaged?
74084.e: The Disability Discrimination Act came into force in 2004. It requires, for example, that public transport and public buildings become accessible without barriers.
74084.m: The Disability Discrimination Act protects people with disabilities from being disadvantaged.

74085.q: What was the system of racial segregation in South Africa called?
74085.e: From 1948 to the early 1990s, apartheid separated people in South Africa by skin colour. Nelson Mandela fought against it and became president in 1994.
74085.m: Apartheid was an unjust system of racial segregation in South Africa.

74086.q: Who gave the famous “I have a dream” speech against racial discrimination in 1963?
74086.e: Martin Luther King spoke in Washington on 28 August 1963 in front of about 250,000 people. He dreamed of a country in which people would not be judged by the colour of their skin.
74086.m: Martin Luther King fought racial discrimination without violence.

74087.q: What is it called when a seemingly neutral rule disadvantages a particular group especially?
74087.e: A rule can sound the same for everyone and still disadvantage one group. An example would be a minimum height for a job where height isn't needed at all.
74087.m: Even seemingly neutral rules can indirectly discriminate against a group.

74088.q: Which Swiss law has been in force since 1996 to promote equality between women and men at work?
74088.e: The Gender Equality Act came into force on 1 July 1996. It forbids, for example, disadvantaging women in pay or promotion.
74088.m: The Gender Equality Act protects against disadvantage at work because of gender.

a: Every person has a worth that nobody may take away
74089.e: Every person has human dignity, regardless of origin, achievement or health. It is the basis of all human rights.
74089.m: Every person has dignity simply because they are human.

74090.q: What does the Swiss Federal Constitution say about human dignity?
a: It must be respected and protected
It only applies to Swiss citizens
It only applies from the age of 18
74090.e: Article 7 stands at the beginning of the fundamental rights in the Federal Constitution. It obliges the state to respect the dignity of every person.
74090.m: The Federal Constitution protects the dignity of every person.

74091.q: How does Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights begin?
a: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights
Everyone has the right to work and pay
No one may be arrested without a reason
Everyone has the right to their own house
74091.e: The first article stresses the equal dignity of all people. The other articles of the Declaration build on it.
74091.m: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.

74092.q: Which action treats a person like a thing and violates their dignity?
74092.e: A person must never be bought or used like an object. The philosopher Immanuel Kant based human dignity on this idea.
74092.m: A person must never be used like a thing.

74093.q: Which act violates human dignity especially seriously and is banned worldwide?
74093.e: Torture destroys a person's physical and mental integrity. It is banned in the Federal Constitution, the European Convention on Human Rights and the UN Convention against Torture.
74093.m: Torture is one of the most serious violations of human dignity.

74094.q: How does Article 1 of the German Basic Law begin?
74094.e: The Basic Law of 1949 puts human dignity in first place. This was a response to the crimes of National Socialism.
74094.m: In the German Basic Law, human dignity comes right at the beginning.

74095.q: Which Swiss organisation did Henri Dunant help to found in order to help wounded people with dignity?
a: The International Committee of the Red Cross
74095.e: Henri Dunant witnessed the Battle of Solferino in 1859 and, with others, founded the Committee in Geneva in 1863. It helps victims of war without distinction.
74095.m: The Red Cross helps all victims of war without distinction.

74096.q: Which organisation adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989?
74096.e: The UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child on 20 November 1989. That is why 20 November is the international day of children's rights.
74096.m: The UN adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989.

74097.q: Up to what age is a person a child according to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?
74097.e: Article 1 of the Convention states that every person under 18 counts as a child. Exceptions are only possible if a country sets the age of majority earlier.
74097.m: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, you are a child until 18.

74098.q: Does the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child also apply in Switzerland?
a: No, it only applies in poor countries
Only in the cantons with big cities
74098.e: Switzerland joined the Convention in 1997. Since then it has had to report regularly on how it puts children's rights into practice.
74098.m: The Convention on the Rights of the Child also applies in Switzerland.

74099.q: Which UN children's fund works for children's rights around the world?
74099.e: UNICEF was founded in 1946 and helps children with health, education and protection. UNESCO, on the other hand, deals with education, science and culture in general.
74099.m: UNICEF is the children's fund of the United Nations.

74100.q: What right do children have in decisions that affect them?
a: The right to give their opinion and be heard
The right to decide everything alone
The right to their own mobile phone
74100.e: Children may give their opinion on all matters that affect them. This opinion must be taken into account according to their age and maturity.
74100.m: Children have the right to give their opinion and be heard.

74101.q: Which right is one of the UN children's rights?
a: The right to play and leisure
74101.e: Article 31 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child protects the right to rest, leisure, play and cultural activities. Playing is important for healthy development.
74101.m: Children have a right to play, leisure and rest.

74102.q: Which principle says that in decisions about children, their well-being must come first?
a: The best interests of the child
74102.e: Article 3 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child requires that the best interests of the child are a primary consideration in all measures. This applies to courts, authorities and schools.
74102.m: In all decisions about children, the best interests of the child must come first.

74103.q: Which country is the only UN member that has not ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (as of 2025)?
74103.e: The USA did sign the Convention in 1995, but never ratified it. All the other UN member states have joined it.
74103.m: Almost every country in the world has ratified the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

74104.q: Which children's right is violated when children have to work in factories instead of going to school?
a: The right to freedom of religion
74104.e: Exploitative child labour stops children from going to school. The Convention on the Rights of the Child protects the right to education and protection from economic exploitation.
74104.m: Child labour often takes away children's right to education.

74105.q: What is an “I” message in an argument?
a: You say how you yourself feel
You only talk about the weather
You give the other person the silent treatment
74105.e: In an “I” message you say, for example: “I get annoyed when you interrupt me.” That way you don't attack the other person and they can listen better.
74105.m: “I” messages describe your own feelings without attacking the other person.

74106.q: What is solving a conflict with the help of a neutral third person called?
74106.e: In mediation, an impartial person helps those who are arguing to find a solution themselves. They don't decide, but guide the conversation.
74106.m: In mediation, a neutral person helps everyone find a solution together.

74107.q: What are pupils called who help sort out arguments between people their own age?
74107.e: Many Swiss schools train children as peacemakers or conflict mediators. They help other children solve conflicts peacefully.
74107.m: Peacemakers help other children solve arguments peacefully.

74108.q: What is a solution called where both sides win?
74108.e: In a win-win solution, the needs of both sides are met. Nobody has to end up as the loser.
74108.m: In a win-win solution, everyone involved benefits.

74109.q: What is an agreement called where each side gives in a little?
74109.e: In a compromise, the people arguing meet in the middle. Each side gives up part of its demands.
74109.m: In a compromise, each side gives in a little.

74110.q: What often happens if you don't sort out an argument early?
74110.e: An unsolved argument can build up step by step until you can hardly talk to each other any more. The earlier you deal with it, the easier it is to solve.
74110.m: The earlier you sort out an argument, the easier the solution.

74111.q: Why is it worth asking about the wishes behind the demands in an argument?
a: It makes it easier to find a solution for both
It means you are sure to win
It means you no longer have to talk to each other
It means the louder one is right
74111.e: Behind a demand there is often a need that can be met in another way. If you know what both sides want, it is easier to find a fair solution.
74111.m: If you understand the wishes behind an argument, it is easier to find a solution.

74112.q: What should you do first in a heated argument?
a: Calm down and get some distance
74112.e: When you are angry, it is hard to listen and think. A short break helps you talk about the problem calmly later.
74112.m: If you calm down first, you can solve an argument better.

74113.q: Which method of resistance did Mahatma Gandhi use in the struggle for India's independence?
74113.e: Gandhi relied on boycotts, marches and civil disobedience without violence. The Salt March of 1930 is well known.
74113.m: Gandhi showed that conflicts can be fought out without violence.

74114.q: Which country has topped the “World Happiness Report” every year since 2018 (as of 2025)?
74114.e: In the World Happiness Report by researchers linked to the UN, Finland has been in first place every year since 2018. Switzerland is usually in the top ten.
74114.m: According to the World Happiness Report, Finland has been the happiest country for years.

74115.q: Which country in the Himalayas measures its success by “Gross National Happiness”?
74115.e: Bhutan puts people's well-being above pure economic growth. Gross National Happiness is even written into its constitution.
74115.m: Bhutan measures prosperity by the happiness of its people.

74116.q: Which animal is a lucky charm at New Year in Switzerland?
74116.e: At New Year, people often give each other little pigs made of marzipan or chocolate. They are supposed to bring luck for the new year.
74116.m: The lucky pig is supposed to bring luck for the new year.

74117.q: Which Greek philosopher called the successful, happy life “eudaimonia”?
74117.e: Aristotle saw eudaimonia as the highest goal of human beings. According to him, you reach it through a virtuous, sensible life.
74117.m: For Aristotle, the happy life was the highest goal.

74118.q: What is the happy feeling called when you are completely absorbed in an activity and forget the time?
74118.e: The term flow was coined by the psychologist Mihály Csíkszentmihályi. Flow often happens when a task is neither too easy nor too hard.
74118.m: In flow, you are so absorbed that you forget the time.

74119.q: Which messenger substance in the brain is often called the “happy hormone”?
74119.e: Serotonin affects mood and well-being. Dopamine and endorphins are also commonly called happy hormones.
74119.m: Serotonin contributes to a good mood.

74120.q: Which plant is a lucky charm when it has four leaves?
74120.e: Clover normally has three leaves. A four-leaf clover is rare and is therefore a symbol of luck.
74120.m: A four-leaf clover is a lucky charm.

74121.q: According to happiness research, what makes people especially happy in the long term?
a: Being alone as much as possible
74121.e: Studies show that friends and family are more important for happiness than possessions. More money only makes people happier as long as they lack what they need.
74121.m: Good relationships make people happy in the long term.

a: Everyone grieves in their own way
Grief always lasts exactly one week
People who are grieving may never laugh
74122.e: Grief can bring sadness, anger, fear or even relief. How long and how strongly someone grieves is very different.

74123.q: Which colour do mourners traditionally wear in Europe?
74123.e: Black has long been the colour of mourning in Europe. In some countries in Asia, white is the colour of mourning instead.
74123.m: In Europe, black is the traditional colour of mourning.

74124.q: What is it called when you express your sympathy to the family of someone who has died?
74124.e: Condolence comes from the Latin condolere, to suffer with. You can offer condolences in person, with a card or in a book of condolence.
74124.m: Offering condolences shows sympathy to those who are grieving.

74125.q: What does it mean when a flag is flown at “half-mast”?
74125.e: When a flag is raised only halfway up the pole, it honours people who have died. This happens, for example, after the death of important people or after disasters.
74125.m: A flag at half-mast is a sign of mourning.

74126.q: What can help children and young people when they are grieving?
a: Talking to someone about their feelings
74126.e: Talking about feelings makes grief easier. Memories such as photos or a visit to the grave can also help.
74126.m: Talking about feelings helps with grief.

74127.q: What is a house called where seriously ill people are cared for at the end of their lives?
74127.e: A hospice offers care, pain relief and support in the last phase of life. Relatives are also supported there.
74127.m: In a hospice, dying people are lovingly cared for.

74128.q: What is the care called that mainly relieves pain for people who cannot be cured?
74128.e: Palliative care no longer aims to cure, but to relieve symptoms and keep quality of life. The term comes from the Latin pallium, cloak.
74128.m: Palliative care relieves suffering when a cure is no longer possible.

74129.q: What is a narrow black band worn as a sign of mourning called?
74129.e: A black armband is worn on the sleeve, or a black ribbon on the lapel. Sportspeople sometimes wear black armbands at matches in memory of someone who has died.
74129.m: A black armband shows that someone is mourning a person.

74131.q: What is the container called in which the ashes of someone who has died are kept?
74131.e: In a cremation, the body is burned at a crematorium. The ashes go into an urn, which can be buried or scattered.
74131.m: The ashes of people who have died are kept in an urn.

74132.q: Which kind of funeral do most people in Switzerland choose today?
74132.e: In Switzerland today, most people who die are cremated. Burial in a coffin has become much rarer.
74132.m: In Switzerland, cremation is the most common.

74133.q: In which country is the “Día de los Muertos”, the Day of the Dead, celebrated colourfully?
74133.e: In Mexico, at the beginning of November, families remember their dead with altars, flowers and sugar skulls. UNESCO counts the festival as intangible cultural heritage.
74133.m: In Mexico, the Day of the Dead is celebrated cheerfully and colourfully.

74134.q: What do visitors traditionally place on a grave in Judaism?
74134.e: Instead of flowers, people in Judaism often place small stones on the grave. They show that someone was there and is thinking of the person who died.
74134.m: In Judaism, people place stones on the grave in remembrance.

74135.q: On which day do Catholic Christians remember their dead on All Souls' Day?
74135.e: All Souls' Day on 2 November follows All Saints' Day. Many people then visit the graves of their relatives and light candles.
74135.m: All Souls' Day on 2 November is a day to remember the dead.

74136.q: On which river in India do many Hindus scatter the ashes of their dead?
74136.e: In Hinduism, people who have died are usually cremated. The Ganges is seen as a holy river, especially in the city of Varanasi.
74136.m: Many Hindus give the ashes of their dead to the Ganges.

74137.q: How is a person who has died traditionally laid in the grave in Islam?
a: With their head towards the west
74137.e: In Islam, the body is wrapped in cloths and buried as soon as possible. The face is turned towards Mecca.
74137.m: In Islam, the person who has died lies with their face towards Mecca.

74138.q: What is a wall with niches for urns called?
74138.e: The word columbarium comes from the Latin columba, dove, because the niches look like dovecotes. Many Swiss cemeteries have such urn walls.
74138.m: In a columbarium, urns are placed in niches.

74139.q: Which colour is traditionally the colour of hope?
74139.e: Green reminds us of things growing and sprouting in spring. That is why it is a symbol of hope and new beginnings.
74139.m: Green is the colour of hope.

74140.q: Which sailors' symbol is a symbol of hope in Christianity?
74140.e: The anchor holds a ship steady in a storm. That is why in the Christian faith it stands as a sign of hope.
74140.m: The anchor is an ancient symbol of hope.

74141.q: Which three virtues does the apostle Paul name together?
74141.e: In the First Letter to the Corinthians, Paul writes about faith, hope and love. They are called the three theological virtues.
74141.m: Faith, love and hope are the three Christian virtues.

74142.q: According to Greek myth, what was left behind in Pandora's box?
74142.e: Pandora opened the jar, and all the evils escaped into the world. Only hope remained inside.
74142.m: Hope was left behind in Pandora's box.

74143.q: Which cape at the southern tip of Africa has hope in its name?
74143.e: The Cape of Good Hope is in South Africa. The name was meant to express hope for a sea route to India.
74143.m: The Cape of Good Hope is in South Africa.

74144.q: Which famous sentence from a 1963 speech by Martin Luther King became a symbol of hope?
74144.e: In Washington in 1963, Martin Luther King spoke of his dream of a society without racial segregation. The speech is a symbol of hope for equal rights.
74144.m: Martin Luther King dreamed of equal rights for all.

74145.q: What is the ability to regain strength after crises called?
74145.e: Resilience means mental toughness. Good relationships and hope help people get through difficult times.
74145.m: Resilient people recover well from crises.

74146.q: What is the attitude called in which you expect good things?
74146.e: Optimists are confident that things will turn out well. The opposite is pessimism.
74146.m: Optimists look to the future with hope.

74147.q: What share of Switzerland's permanent resident population does not have a Swiss passport (as of 2023)?
74147.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, just over 27 per cent of the population have a foreign nationality. Many of them were born in Switzerland or have lived here for decades.
74147.m: About a quarter of the people in Switzerland have a foreign passport.

74148.q: What is it called when all people naturally belong from the start, including those with disabilities?
74148.e: With inclusion, the community adapts so that everyone can take part. With exclusion, people are shut out.
74148.m: Inclusion means that all people belong.

74149.q: What is Swiss German Sign Language?
a: A language of its own with its own grammar
A dot script for blind people
74149.e: Deaf people communicate with their hands, facial expressions and body posture. Sign language has its own grammar and is not simply translated German.
74149.m: Swiss German Sign Language is a language of its own.

74150.q: Which dot script can blind people read with their fingers?
74150.e: Louis Braille developed the script in the 19th century. Each character consists of up to six raised dots.
74150.m: Blind people read Braille with their fingers.

74151.q: What is it called when buildings, transport and websites can be used by everyone without obstacles?
74151.e: Ramps, lifts, tactile guide lines for blind people and easy-to-read websites make things accessible. Older people and parents with pushchairs benefit too.
74151.m: Accessibility makes places and services open to everyone.

74152.q: Which UN agreement on the rights of people with disabilities did Switzerland ratify in 2014?
a: Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
Convention on the Rights of the Child
74152.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities dates from 2006. Switzerland joined it in 2014, committing itself to more participation.
74152.m: In 2014, Switzerland committed itself to the rights of people with disabilities.

74154.q: What are the Olympic Games for athletes with disabilities called?
74154.e: The Paralympics take place shortly after the Olympic Games in the same place. Switzerland regularly wins medals there, for example in wheelchair sports.
74154.m: Athletes with disabilities compete at the Paralympics.

74155.q: Which federal office has been working for equality between women and men since 1988?
74155.e: The Federal Office for Gender Equality (FOGE) belongs to the Federal Department of Home Affairs. It works, for example, for equal pay and against violence.
74155.m: A federal office of its own deals with gender equality.

74156.q: What do working mothers in Switzerland get after the birth of a child?
74156.e: Since 2005, Switzerland has had maternity pay. Working mothers receive part of their wages for 14 weeks.
74156.m: In Switzerland, mothers have 14 weeks of paid maternity leave.

74157.q: On which date did big women's strikes take place in Switzerland in 1991 and 2019?
74157.e: On this day in 1991, and again in 2019, hundreds of thousands of women took to the streets. Among other things, they demanded equal pay.
74157.m: 14 June is the day of the women's strike in Switzerland.

74158.e: International Women's Day on 8 March commemorates the fight for women's rights. It has been marked around the world for more than a hundred years.
74158.m: International Women's Day is on 8 March.

74159.q: How long has paternity leave been in Switzerland since 2021?
74159.e: Voters approved paid paternity leave in September 2020. Since 2021, fathers have been entitled to two weeks.
74159.m: In Switzerland, fathers have two weeks of paternity leave.

74160.q: Which right did women in Switzerland only get at federal level in 1971?
a: The right to vote and stand for election
The right to go to school
The right to ride a bike
74160.e: The men approved women's suffrage in a vote in February 1971. This made Switzerland one of the last countries in Europe to do so.
74160.m: Since 1971, women in Switzerland have been able to vote and stand for election.

a: The same pay for women and men for work of equal value
Women always earn more than men
Pay rises by the same amount every year
74161.e: Women and men should earn the same for work of equal value. This is in the Federal Constitution and the Gender Equality Act.
74161.m: Equal pay means the same pay for work of equal value.

74162.q: Which big tournament, once often seen as something for men, took place in Switzerland in summer 2025?
a: The Men's Ice Hockey World Championship
74162.e: Women's EURO 2025 drew lots of spectators to Swiss stadiums. Football was long seen as a typical men's sport.
74162.m: Sport is for everyone, regardless of gender.

74163.q: What is a man called who mainly runs the household and looks after the children?
74163.e: A house husband takes on the family work, often while his partner goes out to work. This used to be seen as a typical role for women.
74163.m: A house husband looks after the household and children.

74164.q: Which colour was often seen as suitable for little boys around 1900?
74164.e: At that time, pink was seen as the little sister of strong red and therefore as masculine. Pink for girls only became established in the 20th century.
74164.m: Colours for boys and girls are a matter of habit, not nature.

74165.q: What is the picture called of the tasks and behaviour that a society expects of people?
74165.e: Role expectations come from upbringing, the media and tradition. They can change a lot over time.
74165.m: Role expectations show what a society expects of people.

74166.q: What is a job with fewer hours than a full-time job called?
74166.e: In Switzerland, many people work part-time to combine family and work. More and more fathers are cutting their hours to do this.
74166.m: Part-time work helps to combine family and work.

74167.q: What are jobs called that anyone can choose, regardless of gender?
74167.e: Gender-neutral job titles and career choices are meant to give everyone the same chances. Examples are healthcare assistants or IT specialists.
74167.m: Every job should be open to all genders.

74168.q: What is the yearly day called when Swiss children get to know a job beyond the usual gender roles?
74168.e: On National Future Day, children in years 5 to 7 often go to work with a parent. They are meant to discover unusual jobs too.
74168.m: Future Day invites children to discover jobs without gender clichés.

a: Harsh criticism of a piece of work
74169.e: Bullying means that someone is deliberately left out, insulted or attacked over a long time. A single argument is not yet bullying.

74170.q: What is bullying that happens via mobile phones and the internet called?
74170.e: In cyberbullying, people are shown up, for example in chats, with photos or comments. It can go on day and night.
74170.m: Cyberbullying follows victims all the way home.

74171.q: Which language does the word “mobbing”, used for bullying in German, come from?
74171.e: The English verb “to mob” means roughly to crowd round and attack someone. In English, mobbing among children is usually called “bullying”.
74171.m: The word mobbing comes from the English “to mob”.

74172.q: What are the children called who watch bullying but don't step in?
74172.e: Bystanders play an important role: when they take the side of the victims, bullying often loses its power. Getting help is not telling tales.
74172.m: If you see bullying, get help.

74173.q: What helps most to stop bullying in a class?
a: When others stand by the victims and get help
When you wait until it's over
74173.e: Bullying needs bystanders who join in or keep quiet. When others take the side of the victims and tell adults, it loses its power.
74173.m: Against bullying, it helps to stand by the victims and get help.

74174.q: What should victims of cyberbullying do with insulting messages?
74174.e: Screenshots help to show the bullying later to parents, teachers or the police. Afterwards you can block and report the person.
74174.m: With cyberbullying, save evidence and get help.

74175.q: What is bullying by a boss called?
74175.e: In bossing, a boss harasses employees. The term comes from the English word boss.

74176.q: What is a method against bullying at schools called, where nobody is blamed but a solution is found together?
74176.e: In the No Blame Approach, the teacher forms a support group that also includes those involved. The aim is to stop the bullying without punishing anyone.
74176.m: The No Blame Approach looks for solutions rather than culprits.

74177.q: What is it called when pupils are trained to settle arguments between people their own age?
74177.e: Peers are people of the same age. In peer mediation, trained young people help others solve a conflict fairly.
74177.m: In peer mediation, young people settle arguments between people their own age.

74178.q: What are the rules for polite behaviour on the internet called?
74178.e: Netiquette is made up of net and etiquette. It includes staying friendly and not showing others up.
74178.m: Netiquette means politeness on the internet.

74179.q: What is a social media profile called that pretends to be someone else?
74179.e: Behind a fake profile is not the person you see in the pictures. That is why you should be careful with people you meet online.
74179.m: Online, you can never be sure who is behind a profile.

74180.q: From what age are most big social networks allowed according to their rules (as of 2025)?
74180.e: Platforms such as Instagram, TikTok or Snapchat require a minimum age of 13 in their terms of use. Some countries are discussing stricter rules.
74180.m: Most social networks are only allowed from 13.

74181.q: What is one of the most important rules before you post a photo of a friend online?
a: Only post it in the evening
74181.e: Everyone has the right to their own image. That is why you may only publish photos of others with their consent.
74181.m: Only post photos of others with their permission.

74182.q: What is the fear of missing out on something important online called?
74182.e: FOMO stands for “fear of missing out”. It can lead to you constantly looking at your phone.
74182.m: FOMO is the fear of missing out.

74183.q: What should you keep in mind when meeting someone you know from online for the first time?
a: Meet in a public place with your parents' knowledge
Meet alone at the person's home
Meet late in the evening without your phone
74183.e: You can't be sure who is behind an online profile. Meeting in a busy place, ideally with someone else, protects you.
74183.m: Only meet people you know from online safely and with your parents' knowledge.

74184.q: What is an online environment called in which you see almost only opinions that match your own?
74184.e: Algorithms often show posts that match what you already like. This creates a filter bubble, and other points of view disappear.
74184.m: In a filter bubble, you hardly see other opinions.

74185.q: What is a deliberate break from your phone and social media called?
74185.e: In a digital detox, you go without digital devices for a while. Many people find it good for real meetings with friends.
74185.m: A break from screens is called a digital detox.

74186.q: What is a scam called in which a message tries to trick you into entering passwords?
74186.e: Phishing messages often look real, for example like a message from a friend or a bank. Never give away passwords, not even to friends.
74186.m: Never give away passwords, not even to friends.

74187.q: What is the principle called in which working people pay the pensions of the older generation with their contributions?
74187.e: The AHV (old-age insurance) works on a pay-as-you-go basis. Working people finance today's pensions and later receive pensions themselves from younger people.
74187.m: In the intergenerational contract, the young provide for the old.

74188.q: What does the AHV in Switzerland mainly pay out?
74188.e: The old-age and survivors' insurance pays pensions to retired people and to surviving relatives. It is the most important pillar of pension provision.
74188.m: The AHV pays pensions for older people.

74189.q: What are the large generations born after the Second World War called?
74189.e: After 1945, a great many children were born in many countries. These baby boomers are now retiring.
74189.m: The baby boomers are the large post-war generation.

74190.q: What is the generation called that was born roughly between 1997 and 2012?
74190.e: Generation Z grew up with smartphones and the internet. It is followed by Generation Alpha.
74190.m: Generation Z grew up with smartphones.

74191.q: Which Swiss foundation has worked for older people since 1917?
74191.e: Pro Senectute offers advice, courses and support for older people. The name is Latin and means “for old age”.
74191.m: Pro Senectute helps older people in Switzerland.

74192.q: What is a house called where young and old deliberately live together and help each other?
74192.e: In a multi-generation house, older people help, for example, with looking after children, and younger people with shopping. That way all generations benefit.
74192.m: In a multi-generation house, young and old live together.

74193.q: What is an argument called that arises because old and young have different values?
74193.e: Each generation grows up in different conditions. This can lead to disagreements, for example about fashion, music or technology.
74193.m: A generation conflict arises from the different values of young and old.

a: People born at about the same time
People who live in the same country
People who have the same job
People who have the same name
74194.e: A generation includes people of a similar age. Children, parents and grandparents belong to three different generations.
74194.m: A generation is people of about the same age.

74195.q: How can a volunteering certificate help young people?
a: To show voluntary work in job applications
To travel by train without a ticket
To be allowed to drive earlier
74195.e: A volunteering certificate confirms voluntary activities, tasks and hours. That way, for example, companies offering apprenticeships can see where someone has helped out.
74195.m: The volunteering certificate confirms voluntary work.

74196.q: What is the short name of the Swiss youth organisation formed from Jungwacht and Blauring?
74196.e: In Jubla, young adults run group sessions and camps for children on a voluntary basis. The organisation has a church background.
74196.m: In Jubla, young leaders volunteer for children.

74197.q: What is typical of voluntary work?
a: You help others without being paid for it
The state forces you to do it
You get paid like in a job
You only work for your own benefit
74197.e: Volunteers give their time unpaid for others, for example in a club or in the neighbourhood. Every year the UN thanks them with a day of their own.
74197.m: Volunteers help others without being paid.

74198.q: What is the Swiss system called in which citizens hold public offices alongside their jobs?
74198.e: In Switzerland, many local councillors, firefighters and members of parliament do this alongside their jobs. This militia system depends on people getting involved.
74198.m: In the militia system, citizens take on public tasks on the side.

74199.q: What is an unpaid position, for example on the committee of a club, called?
74199.e: Volunteers receive no wages, at most a small allowance. They help out in sports clubs, churches or social organisations.
74199.m: A voluntary post is done without pay.

74200.q: Which youth organisation with neckerchiefs is largely run by young volunteers in Switzerland?
74200.e: In the Scouts, older young people run the groups for the younger ones on a voluntary basis. Their founder was the Briton Robert Baden-Powell.
74200.m: The Scouts are run by young volunteers.

74201.q: What counts as informal voluntary work?
a: Helping your neighbour with her shopping
74201.e: Informal voluntary work happens outside clubs, for example as help between neighbours. Formal voluntary work takes place in organisations.
74201.m: Helping your neighbours is also valuable voluntary work.

74202.q: Which organisation in Switzerland uses volunteers to hand out surplus food to people living in poverty?
74202.e: Tischlein deck dich saves food from being thrown away. Volunteers pass it on to people affected by poverty.
74202.m: Tischlein deck dich saves food for people in need.

74203.q: Which nature conservation organisation was founded in 1961 in Morges on Lake Geneva?
74203.e: The WWF has its international headquarters in Gland in the canton of Vaud. Its symbol is the giant panda.
74203.m: The WWF was founded in Switzerland in 1961.

74204.q: What should you do before getting a pet?
a: Only pay attention to how it looks
74204.e: Every animal needs suitable food, enough space, things to do and often others of its kind. If you sort this out beforehand, you can look after the animal well.
74204.m: Before getting a pet, find out about its needs.

74205.q: Why are you not allowed to keep a guinea pig on its own in Switzerland?
74205.e: The Swiss Animal Protection Ordinance requires sociable animals like guinea pigs to have contact with others of their kind. Kept alone, they suffer from the lack of company.
74205.m: Sociable animals need others of their kind.

74206.q: Which term does the Swiss Federal Constitution use to protect animals and plants?
74206.e: In 1992, Switzerland was one of the first countries to put the dignity of living beings into its constitution. The Animal Protection Act expressly protects the dignity of animals.
74206.m: Switzerland protects the dignity of living beings in its constitution.

74207.q: What does the “3R principle” for animal experiments stand for?
74207.e: Animal experiments should be replaced, reduced and made gentler wherever possible.
74207.m: The 3R principle aims to replace, reduce and improve animal experiments.

a: Keeping animals in a way that meets their needs
As many animals as possible in a small space
Only showing animals in the zoo
